Font objects

Source: R/zz-gen-shared.R
go_font.Rd

Used for font, insidetextfont, tickfont, outsidetextfont, textfont, labelfont, grouptitlefont, rangefont in 296 places in the schema. go_font() creates one; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_font(
  ...,
  color = NULL,
  family = NULL,
  lineposition = NULL,
  shadow = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  style = NULL,
  textcase = NULL,
  variant = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

...

Not for properties, which must be named in full: an abbreviated or unknown name is an error that suggests the right one.

color

Color: a CSS color string or R color name. In some contexts: Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

family

HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available. String. In some contexts: String, or a vector of these. Not available in every context.

lineposition

Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an "under", "over" or "through" as well as combinations e.g. "under+over", etc. Any combination of "under", "over", "through" joined with "+", or one of "none". In some contexts: Any combination of "under", "over", "through" joined with "+", or one of "none", or a vector of these. Not available in every context.

shadow

Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. "auto" places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options. String. In some contexts: String, or a vector of these. Not available in every context.

size

Number in the interval [1, Inf]. In some contexts: Number in the interval [1, Inf], or a vector of these. Not available in every context.

style

Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family. One of "normal", "italic". In some contexts: One of "normal", "italic", or a vector of these. Not available in every context.

textcase

Sets capitalization of text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized. One of "normal", "word caps", "upper", "lower". In some contexts: One of "normal", "word caps", "upper", "lower", or a vector of these. Not available in every context.

variant

Sets the variant of the font. One of "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "all-petite-caps", "petite-caps", "unicase". In some contexts: One of "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "all-petite-caps", "petite-caps", "unicase", or a vector of these; or One of "normal", "small-caps", or a vector of these. Not available in every context.

weight

Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. Integer in the interval [1, 1000]. In some contexts: Integer in the interval [1, 1000], or a vector of these; or One of "normal", "bold", or a vector of these. Not available in every context.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_font object (a named list).

Details

These objects appear in 296 places in the plotly.js schema (properties named font, insidetextfont, tickfont, outsidetextfont, textfont, labelfont, grouptitlefont, rangefont), with small differences between them: for example, not every context has every property below. go_font() checks the values against the contexts it can be used in; when the object is placed in a figure it is checked again against that context's rules.

Examples

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, mode = "markers") |>
  update_layout(font = go_font(color = "red"))
